messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — Sev1 routing anomaly detected: spikes in latency and 5xxs for 'hosted' tier; unusual upstream routing to dedicated pools observed at 18:00 UTC. auto-attach: #incidents, paging oncall.

oncall-sre: I'm on it, joining now. what are the affected tenants?

maya: seeing errors for tenant: acme-payments and tenant: bluewave in hosted region-us-west-2. latency jumped 10x, errors ~40% for last 3m. Grafana: https://grafana.example/r/abcd1234

alex: logs show requests labelled hosted_tier but bound to pool=dedi-pool-42 and model_variant=redwood-large-quant. That pool is intended for dedicated customers only.

jin: quick grep of routing-policy change history -> 17:56 UTC policy update (PR #4921) introduced a rule that uses `tenant_label` anchor. suspect anchor resolution error.

maya: can we see the policy snippet?

jin: pasted below:

```json
# routing policy excerpt (simplified)
- id: policy-anch-327
  match:
    - condition: "resource.tier == 'hosted' && template.anchor in tenant.labels"
      action: bind_pool('dedicated-*:pool')
```

jin: The `template.anchor in tenant.labels` is evaluating differently for some hosted tenants that have a legacy label `bridge:true`. That label matches the anchor value and triggers the dedicated bind.

alex: confirms: tenant acme-payments has label `bridge:true` from an old onboarding script. so hosted traffic is being misrouted to dedicated.

sam: customer-impact summary so far: ~3.2k requests/min spilled to dedicated pool, median latency increased from 40ms -> 420ms for those requests, error rate from 0.5% -> 36%. billing/profile unaffected, no credential leakage. customers experiencing timeouts and partial failures.

oncall-sre: mitigation plan: 1) throttle traf to dedi-pool, 2) rollback policy change to previous commit, 3) create temporary override rule to force hosted->hosted. who can run rollback?

ops-bot: Action queued: deploy rollback policy-anch-327 -> v1.17. Running in 30s. will post status.

incident-bot: deploy job started: deploy/rollback-policy-327 (ci-run-8801).

ops-bot: rollback complete. policy-anch-327 reverted to v1.16 at 18:08 UTC.

alex: I'm seeing traffic reflowing to hosted pools now. error rate dropping. confirming with ingress logs.

maya: can we also patch the policy expression to avoid anchor ambiguity? Jin, can you propose a fix?

jin: proposed change: require explicit label key match and type check: `resource.tier == 'hosted' && tenant.labels['bridge'] == 'true' && tenant.binding == 'bridge-enabled'` — or better: avoid binding to `dedicated-*` unless tenant.has_dedicated_contract == true. will open PR with tests.

sam: ops note: temporary quota set on dedi-pool-42 to 5% of normal throughput to avoid any residual spill.

oncall-sre: customers impacted notified? CS notified us: @cs-team has sent blameless status to affected accounts and asked for ETA.

maya: timeline: incident opened 18:00 UTC, rollback at 18:08 UTC, majority of traffic normalized by 18:12 UTC.

alex: current metrics: hosted 5xxs down to 1.2% (from 36%), p50 latency back to 48ms. will monitor for 30m.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigated, monitoring. severity: P1 -> P2.

oncall-sre: declaring incident resolved at 18:30 UTC pending postmortem. assigning follow-up items:
- jin: policy PR + unit tests + integration test verifying label anchors (due EOD)
- alex: run tenant inventory to find other tenants with `bridge:true` tag and flag for cleanup (due 24h)
- maya: add canary/rollout guard to policy deploy pipeline (1% -> 10% -> 100%) and add automated alert if dedicated bind increases >2% of hosted traffic (due 72h)
- sam: customer impact doc + timeline + sent updates to affected customers (done)

maya: short-term postmortem link: https://notebook.example/incident/1809991234/pm-draft

alex: logs export: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/1809991234/*.gz

ops-bot: reminder: please add runbook entry under docs/ops/runbooks/routing-policy-anchors.md

jin: PR opened: https://git.example/redwood/routing/pulls/4980 (includes unit tests and explicit label key check).

maya: great job triaging. adding :thumbsup: reactions. will keep thread open for final signoff after 24h monitoring.

sam: final note: no data exfiltration, root cause: ambiguous anchor semantics + legacy tenant label. mitigation: policy rollback + quota + code fix + tenant cleanup.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (mitigated) — thread archived in 7d.
